name: Permissions-Policy introspection and reporting
plain: A page can list which browser features it is allowed to use, and a server can hear about violations.
meaning: document.permissionsPolicy.features() returns every feature the browser knows, and allowedFeatures() the ones this frame may use. Permissions-Policy-Report-Only lets a server learn what a page would break. Feature-Policy is the legacy name.

chrome.note: Header from 85; document.permissionsPolicy introspection from 152 per compat data

edge.note: Header from 85; document.permissionsPolicy introspection from 152 per compat data

safari.note: No Permissions-Policy header or introspection API in compat data

firefox.note: No Permissions-Policy header or introspection API in compat data

chrome_android.note: Header from 85; document.permissionsPolicy introspection from 152 per compat data

data.metric: A page can list which browser features it is allowed to use, and a server can hear about violations.

limits.headline: Can list the features this page may use, and learn which ones it is blocked from
limits.user_action: None, the page reads it silently
can: List all policy controlled features in Chromium
Tell which features a frame may use
limits.differs: Chromium implements it. Safari and Firefox are partial or absent. Report only and Document-Policy are low confidence.

story.what_it_is: The page can read the rule list that decides which browser powers its frames may use.

marketing.name: Permissions Policy
marketing.pitch: The standard for controlling which features a page and its frames can use.

story.for_you: This is about what a page and the ads in it are allowed to do. You rarely see it.
story.for_makers: Makers lock down embedded frames and check their own policy at run time.

use_cases.example: A shop blocks camera and microphone access for embedded ads.
A publisher checks which features its ad frames may use.

risks: The feature list is itself a browser version signal

technical_bounds: Document-Policy and Feature-Policy details are low confidence
